content.comment_body: Hello. I have a [product_name] device connected at home for heating and some lights, and it has stopped working. I can't upload the program to it. The software doesn't recognize it, but when scanning for devices, it finds the factory IP address, likely because the device reset itself. However, when I ping the device, there is no response, while my other two devices work fine. I don't know what to do next and hope I won't need to buy a replacement. Is there any firmware or SD card method to restore it? Any help would be appreciated.
You posted in the German-speaking section of the forum. The moderator will move your topic to the English-speaking section tomorrow. Please write your future posts in English. Thank you.

I've never seen a [product_name] device reset itself to factory settings. What IP address does your device currently show, 192.168.0.3? What is your PC or laptop's IP address? Do you have a backup copy of the program?

analysis.insight_summary: Users report unexpected malfunction of the [product_name] device, with a sudden reset to factory settings causing loss of access to the program. The device becomes unresponsive to network pings, though other similar devices remain reachable. Users are concerned about needing hardware replacement and seek solutions such as firmware recovery or restoring the device via SD card, showing concerns about device reliability and data integrity.
analysis.user_expectations: [product_name] device should function reliably without self-resets and include straightforward recovery options using SD card or firmware restoration. Users want to restore functionality without replacing hardware.
